description: MovingPandas is a Python library for movement data exploration and analysis. It provides trajectory data structures and functions for handling movement data built on pandas, GeoPandas and HoloViz, so point records from GPS loggers, vehicle fleets or AIS ship messages can be turned into trajectories, split, generalised, cleaned, aggregated and plotted. The project is maintained by the MovingPandas developers and was reviewed by pyOpenSci; the README carries a repostatus badge marking it as active. Coverage is generic: it works on any movement data the user supplies, from a single city to global shipping tracks. Access: source code on GitHub, releases on PyPI and conda-forge, and documentation on Read the Docs. Licence and cost: BSD 3-Clause, free. Caveats: it is a library, not a dataset, so results depend on the quality and sampling of the input points, and very large AIS or GPS archives need chunking because the data structures sit in memory. It serves as a data preparation step for traffic and vessel flow analysis, calibration of agent-based models and exposure studies that overlay trajectories on hazards, and pairs with AIS sources in the catalogue such as the NOAA Marine Cadastre AIS data and the Danish Maritime Authority AIS data.
